solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Plant is found in hard ground east of Hackney?

indicators.note: in an across answer east is to the right, so this piece follows the other one

parts.note: a hackney is a breed of horse, also a horse for hire

indicators.note: a thing found in another sits inside it, so one piece goes within the other
something ground has been crushed and broken up, so the letters beside it are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, then rearranged
taken as written, placed inside the rearranged letters

explanation.surface: A gardener finds a plant growing in the hard ground of east London, near Hackney.
explanation.walkthrough: Hackney looks like the London borough, but here it is a kind of horse; 'east of' just puts the root after it in an across answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Horseradish is a plant whose pungent root is grated to make a sauce.

clue.text: Dislike looking after the Spanish Prime Minister's wife

indicators.note: someone looking after another wraps protection around them, so one piece goes around the rest

parts.note: to dislike strongly is to hate
el is Spanish for the
PM is the usual abbreviation for Prime Minister

explanation.surface: Someone dislikes the wife of the Spanish prime minister.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as one long phrase about a Spanish leader's spouse; only the last word is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A helpmate is a companion and helper, traditionally used of a spouse, especially a wife.

clue.text: Show catalogue to make an impression

definitions.meaning: second meaning: an official list or record
third meaning: to sink in or be noticed

explanation.surface: An exhibition catalogue is designed to make an impression on visitors.
explanation.walkthrough: This is a triple definition: three separate senses of one word, each a stand-alone phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: The word works as a verb for displaying a feeling, a noun for an official list, and a verb for getting noticed.

clue.text: Conclusion of the three R's contains nothing wrong

definitions.note: a noun here: a wrong, a mistake

indicators.note: the conclusion of a word is its final letter, so only that is kept

parts.note: the final letter of the

indicators.note: contains says one piece holds another inside it

parts.note: taken literally, three copies of the letter R
nothing is zero, which looks like the letter O

explanation.surface: Teaching reading, writing and arithmetic is concluded to contain nothing wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: The three R's are reading, writing and arithmetic, but here they are just three letter Rs, with O slipped between the second and third.
explanation.definitionFit: An error is a mistake, the noun sense of a wrong.

clue.text: Friendly Island having to level up

indicators.note: in a down answer, going up means the letters read from bottom to top
a thing having another holds it, so one piece sits inside the island

parts.note: Elba is the Mediterranean island of Napoleon's exile
to level a gun is to aim it

explanation.surface: A friendly island community is having to level up its economy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Level up' reads as one modern phrase, but level is the verb aim and up turns the whole construction over.
explanation.definitionFit: Amiable means good-natured and pleasant, a close synonym for friendly.

clue.text: Examine popular way to retain muscle

parts.note: something popular is in

indicators.note: to retain something is to keep hold of it, so one piece is held inside another

parts.note: ST is street, a way
a pec is a chest muscle, short for pectoral

explanation.surface: A trainer examines the popular way to keep muscle on.
explanation.definitionFit: To inspect is to look at closely, a direct synonym for examine.

clue.text: Bring her a dire warning of things to come?

indicators.note: dire means dreadful or in a bad state, so the letters are left in a mess and rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone is told to bring a woman a grave warning about the future.
explanation.definitionFit: A harbinger is a herald or omen, something that announces what is coming.

clue.text: Politician receives answer and guidance on this issue

indicators.note: one who receives something takes it in, so a piece goes inside the politician

parts.note: MP is a Member of Parliament
A is the standard abbreviation for answer

explanation.surface: A politician gets a reply and some advice about a current issue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Issue' sounds like a political matter, but it can be read as this edition of the paper: a map is guidance to wherever you are going.
explanation.definitionFit: A map gives direction to a traveller, so it is a form of guidance; the definition is loose and playful.

clue.text: Handy reference work

definitions.meaning: second meaning: a handbook of instructions

explanation.walkthrough: Handy reads as describing a useful reference book, but it is a separate meaning: relating to the hand.
explanation.definitionFit: Manual as an adjective means operated by hand, and as a noun it is an instruction book.

clue.text: Whistleblower overwhelmed by a favour

indicators.note: something overwhelmed is engulfed and swallowed up, so it sits inside the other piece

parts.note: per means a or each, as in miles per hour
a referee blows a whistle

explanation.surface: A whistleblower is swamped by someone doing them a favour.
explanation.walkthrough: Whistleblower suggests an informant, but it is a football referee.
explanation.definitionFit: To prefer someone is to favour them over others.

clue.text: He won't keep up without a good drink

indicators.note: without means lacking, so a letter is taken away

parts.note: one who lags behind cannot keep up
G is short for good

explanation.surface: A man who can't hold his drink won't keep up without a good one.
explanation.walkthrough: The opening phrase is a cryptic description of a straggler; removing one G from it leaves the beer.
explanation.definitionFit: Lager is a light, fizzy beer, so it is a drink.

clue.text: Criminal runs a nice protection racket?

indicators.note: criminal means crooked or bent, so the following letters are twisted into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: A gangster operates a cosy little extortion scheme.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags a cynical joke: insurance is protection one pays for, and some would call it a racket.
explanation.definitionFit: Insurance gives financial cover against loss, so it is protection, wryly cast as a racket.

clue.text: Extremely poor novel bares images about nurses

indicators.note: about means turned round, so the letters are read backwards
to nurse is to hold close, so the phrase cradles the answer within its letters

parts.note: the run of letters in the middle of these words

explanation.surface: A poor-quality novel exposes pictures of nurses.
explanation.walkthrough: Nurses looks like hospital staff but is the verb holding the answer; the run is found backwards, so read right to left through 'novel bares images'.
explanation.definitionFit: Miserable can mean wretchedly inadequate, as in a miserable wage, so extremely poor.

clue.text: Enraged criminal loses head

indicators.note: losing its head means the word drops its first letter

parts.note: a pirate is a criminal at sea

explanation.surface: An enraged criminal is beheaded.
explanation.definitionFit: Irate means very angry, a direct synonym for enraged.

clue.text: Two articles, first of them about dramatic location

parts.note: the definite and indefinite articles, the and a

indicators.note: first of means only the opening letter of the next word is used

parts.note: the opening letter of them
re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: An essay on two articles, the first concerning a dramatic place.
explanation.definitionFit: A theatre is the building where plays are staged, the location of drama.

clue.text: What may cause pain, besides face fungus round top of head?

definitions.note: toothache is itself pain; the definition is loose

parts.note: too means as well, besides

indicators.note: round means surrounding, so one piece wraps around the letter

parts.note: facial hair jokingly called fungus; tache is short for moustache

indicators.note: the top of a word in a down answer is its first letter

parts.note: the opening letter of head

explanation.surface: Some bother causing pain, along with a moustache growing around the head.
explanation.walkthrough: Face fungus is jocular British slang for a beard or moustache.
explanation.definitionFit: Toothache is pain in a tooth, and the clue loosely treats it as a source of suffering.

clue.text: Adult understood revolutionary outfit consigned to history

indicators.note: a revolution turns things round, so the letters are read backwards

parts.note: A is the film rating for adult
to have got something is to have understood it

explanation.surface: A grown-up grasped that a revolutionary costume belongs in the past.
explanation.walkthrough: Revolutionary seems to describe the outfit, but it turns the letters round.
explanation.definitionFit: The toga was the robe worn in ancient Rome, a garment long out of use.

clue.text: District and possibly Victoria blocked by Circle Line

definitions.note: an adjective here, describing a district

indicators.note: possibly signals that Victoria is one example of the wider title
something blocked has an obstruction lodged inside it

parts.note: Regina means queen; Queen Victoria signed Victoria Regina
a circle is shaped like the letter O
L is short for line

explanation.surface: The District and Victoria London Underground lines are held up by the Circle line.
explanation.walkthrough: District, Victoria and Circle are all London Underground lines, but only District is the definition, used as an adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Regional means relating to a region or district, so it describes a district.

clue.text: City's exclusion zone?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a city in the English Midlands
second meaning: from the idiom of sending someone to it, meaning to ostracise them

explanation.walkthrough: To send someone to Coventry is a British idiom for refusing to speak to them, so the city figuratively becomes a place of exclusion.
explanation.definitionFit: The answer is a real Midlands city, and through the idiom also the place where shunned people are figuratively sent.

clue.text: Othello possibly offers something extra for audience

indicators.note: an audience listens, so the word is chosen for its sound rather than spelling

parts.note: something extra is more

explanation.surface: An actor playing Othello offers a little extra for the theatre audience.
explanation.walkthrough: Othello, Shakespeare's title character, is a Moor; possibly marks him as one example.
explanation.definitionFit: Othello is described in the play as a Moor, a North African, so he is one example.

clue.text: Reintroduce subject of wage increase for salesman?

parts.note: a rep is a sales representative
a rise is a pay increase in British usage

explanation.surface: A salesman brings up the topic of a pay rise again.
explanation.walkthrough: The wordplay reads as a rise for a rep, so the salesman's piece comes first. A rise is the British term for a raise in pay.
explanation.definitionFit: To reprise is to repeat a theme or piece of music, bringing it back again.

clue.text: Destroy abandoned depot sheltering men

indicators.note: sheltering means protecting inside, so the scrambled word holds another piece
something abandoned is left in disorder, so the letters are scrambled

parts.note: taken as written, then rearranged
OR is other ranks, ordinary soldiers

explanation.surface: Bomb a disused depot where soldiers are hiding.
explanation.definitionFit: To torpedo something is to wreck it, figuratively as well as with a missile.

clue.text: This evening is in honour of lady's champion we hear

indicators.note: we hear says the words are judged by their sound when spoken

parts.note: to someone is the form of a toast in their honour, and a knight fights for his lady's honour

explanation.surface: A celebration this evening honours a lady's champion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'To knight' sounds like the answer; the silent K disappears in speech.
explanation.definitionFit: Tonight refers to the present or coming evening.

clue.text: Virtuous Catholic experiences beginnings of titillating emotions

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for Catholic
to have a feeling is to experience it

indicators.note: beginnings means just the first letter of each following word

parts.note: opening letters of both words

explanation.surface: A devout Catholic feels the first stirrings of arousal.
explanation.definitionFit: Chaste means sexually pure, a sense of virtuous.

clue.text: This attack could be made faster

indicators.note: could be made says the answer can be formed by rearranging the word that follows

parts.note: taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: The assault could be done more quickly.
explanation.definitionFit: To strafe is to attack with gunfire from low-flying aircraft.

clue.text: Shelter children's pets here

parts.note: a hut is a simple shelter
ch is short for children or child

explanation.surface: Children keep their pets in a shelter.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as one phrase about a pet house; the wordplay is split off at the start.
explanation.definitionFit: A hutch is a wooden cage in which rabbits and other small pets are kept.

clue.text: Severely criticise book about author's show

parts.note: critics pan a poor show

indicators.note: about means around, so the book wraps the next piece

parts.note: a tome is a large book
the author speaking of themselves says I'm, the setter's I am

explanation.surface: A critic slams a book about a writer's stage show.
explanation.walkthrough: Pantomime is the British Christmas stage show for families, with slapstick, songs and audience participation.
explanation.definitionFit: A pantomime is a theatrical entertainment, so it is a type of show.

clue.text: Instruct marshal to request fellowship

definitions.meaning: second meaning: to arrange in sequence
third meaning: to ask for, as food in a restaurant
fourth meaning: a religious or chivalric society

explanation.surface: An official instructs a marshal to ask for companionship.
explanation.walkthrough: This is a quadruple definition: four separate senses of one five-letter word.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means to command, to put in sequence, to ask for, and a brotherhood such as a monastic society.

clue.text: He's caring, busy and thorough

indicators.note: busy suggests bustling activity, so the letters are moved about

parts.note: taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: A description of a person: kind, active and meticulous.
explanation.definitionFit: A searching examination is one that is penetrating and leaves nothing out.

clue.text: Get very angry having lost one's cake

indicators.note: having lost means a part is gone, so those letters are removed

parts.note: the British idiom do one's nut means fly into a rage
taken as written; these are the letters removed

explanation.surface: Someone flies into a rage after losing their cake.
explanation.walkthrough: To do one's nut is British slang for losing one's temper.
explanation.definitionFit: A donut is the American spelling of doughnut, a ring-shaped fried cake.

clue.text: Scrutinise opening of sewer

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to look at closely
second meaning: the hole in a needle, a sewer being something that sews

explanation.walkthrough: Sewer suggests a drain, but it is read as one who sews: a needle, whose opening takes the thread.
explanation.definitionFit: To eye is to watch closely, and the eye of a needle is the hole for the thread.

clue.text: Head of Engineering and Reader form union by means of a vote

indicators.note: the head of a word is its opening letter

parts.note: opening letter of Engineering
a lector is a reader, especially of lessons in church
to ally is to join together

explanation.surface: An engineering department head and a university reader form a union through a ballot.
explanation.walkthrough: A Reader is a senior university lecturer in Britain, but here the word means a lector, one who reads aloud in church.
explanation.definitionFit: Electorally means through elections, so by voting.
